title: Dock
summary: A workspace of panels (Toolbox | Canvas | Properties) laid out as a tree of resizable splits and tab groups. Drag a separator or use its arrow keys to resize, choose a tab to switch a group, drag a panel's header or tab onto another group (its center to add as a tab, an edge to split and dock there) or use a group's Move button to do the same without a mouse, Close/reopen a panel from the toolbar's Panels menu, or use a single-panel header's chevron to collapse it to just its title. A collapsed group at a screen edge folds to a narrow rail button instead; activating it opens the panel as a flyout over the content, closing on Escape, an outside click or a blur. The flyout opens with an Expand button ahead of the panel's own content: activating it restores the panel to a normal docked header - a different, clearly separate action from opening or closing the flyout itself, and the only click path back from a collapsed rail short of reloading or clearing a persistKey-backed store. A toolbar-start slot lets a host add its own menus (File/Edit/View-style) alongside it - the dock draws none of that content itself. The layout can be saved and restored across reloads through persistKey. The arrangement is one JSON layout document you can read, store and set. Free-running by default (a change applies right away, then fires pk-layout-change); a host that wants every change to round-trip first sets confirmLayout(arg) as a callback property (business logic, not config data, like pk-tool-page's run) - arg is { layout: json, reason }, and the settled result (a layout JSON string, or null/undefined to keep the previous one) is what gets applied and reported. Step 2 of #432: docked panels, move, drag-to-dock, close/reopen, header-collapse, collapse-to-rail and its Expand affordance (#636), and persistence; floating panels (model operations landed, no UI yet) and a pk-dock-panel element come in later steps.

props.name: layout
props.description: The arrangement: { version, seq, root, collapsed } where root is a split { id, type: 'split', orientation, size, min, max, a, b } or a tab group { id, type: 'tabs', active, panels }, and collapsed is the list of open panel ids folded to their header. Leave it unset for the default arrangement derived from each panel's data-group. The element validates what it is given (panels that are not declared are dropped, panels the layout lacks are added, bad numbers are repaired). While the user resizes, chooses a tab or collapses a panel the element owns it; after pk-layout-change the host does. Property or a JSON attribute.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of a tab group (aria-label), for example the workspace's name. A single-panel group is named by its heading.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of every separator between two panels (aria-label).

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill the height the parent gives it (a parent with a definite height, or a flex or grid parent) instead of --pk-dock-height.

props.name: persistKey
props.description: Save and restore the layout across reloads, through the SDK's store (js/store.js), under the key pk-dock:<persistKey>. Leave unset to disable persistence. On connect, a saved layout is used as the initial arrangement when the layout prop is not set (stored data wins over the default arrangement); every later pk-layout-change (resize, activate, panels) is saved, but a layout the host sets is not. Give each pk-dock on a page its own value; changing it starts a fresh, separately-saved layout.

slots.name: <panel id>
slots.description: One panel: any element with slot="<id>" (a lowercase id, letters, digits, - and _, up to 40 characters). data-heading is its title (the id when missing) and data-group (left, center, right, bottom) places it in the default arrangement. Panels are slotted, never moved, so a form or a scroll position inside one survives resizing and switching tabs.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown when there is no panel.

slots.name: toolbar-start
slots.description: The start of the toolbar (part toolbar), before the dock's own Panels menu: a place for a host app's own top-level menus (File, Edit, View...). The dock draws none of this; it only gives it a stable spot next to its own controls. The toolbar shows whenever this slot holds something or a panel is closed, and collapses away when both are empty.

events.name: pk-layout-change
events.description: The arrangement changed because of the user or because panels were added or removed: reason is resize (a drag ended or a key moved a separator), activate (a tab was chosen), move (a panel was moved to another group from its Move menu or a pointer drag), collapse (a single-panel header's chevron toggled its body) or panels (the declared panels changed and the layout was repaired). layout is the new document. Not raised for a layout the host set, nor for the first render. Not cancelable.

parts.name: toolbar
parts.description: The bar above the tree: slot toolbar-start (a host app's own menus) then the dock's own Panels menu. Collapses away while both are empty.

parts.name: root
parts.description: The frame that holds the rendered tree.

parts.name: group
parts.description: One tab group or single panel, with its header.

parts.name: header
parts.description: The title bar of a single-panel group.

parts.name: collapse-toggle
parts.description: The button in a single-panel header that collapses or expands its body. Reused (same part and class) for the flyout's own Expand button (issue #636), which restores the panel to a normal docked header - a different action from the rail button that opened the flyout, which only opens or closes it.

parts.name: title
parts.description: The panel's heading text inside collapse-toggle.

parts.name: body
parts.description: The scrolling area around a panel's content.

parts.name: rail-button
parts.description: The button a collapsed edge group folds to instead of a header; opens the panel as a flyout.

parts.name: flyout
parts.description: The floating layer a rail button opens its panel into, positioned next to the button. Its Expand button (part collapse-toggle, issue #636) comes first, ahead of the panel's own content.

parts.name: status
parts.description: The visually hidden live region that announces a move.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-height
cssProperties.description: Height when fill is not set.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-header-height
cssProperties.description: Minimum height of a single-panel header.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-rail-width
cssProperties.description: Width of a collapsed edge group's rail button.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-flyout-width
cssProperties.description: Width of the flyout a rail button opens.

a11y: Each separator is a pk-splitter: role=separator with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and its own arrow keys (Left and Right side by side, mirrored in a right-to-left page; Up and Down stacked; Home and End), so every resize has a keyboard path. A group of several panels is a pk-tabs tablist (roving tabindex, arrow keys); a single panel is a labelled section named by its heading. Hidden tab panels are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree. When there is more than one group, its header (or its tab strip, in the trailing slot) carries a Move button (a pk-dropdown, reachable by Tab and opened with Enter or Space) listing every other group: Add as tab in it, or Dock left/right/above/below it; choosing one moves the active panel with dockPanel/moveTab and moves focus to it, and the visually hidden status part announces the result. A pointer can instead drag a header or tab onto another group's center (add as tab) or an edge (split and dock there), shown with an accent drop-zone highlight while dragging; this calls the same dockPanel/moveTab operations and is purely additive - the Move menu keeps working unchanged and needs no mouse. A single-panel header's collapse-toggle is a native button (Tab to reach it, Enter or Space to activate, no extra key handling needed) with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the body it hides; a tab group does not offer collapse yet. A collapsed group at a screen edge is instead a rail button (also a native button, same Enter/Space activation) with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded naming the flyout it opens; the flyout closes and returns focus to the rail button on Escape, and closes (without moving focus) on an outside pointerdown or when focus leaves it. The flyout opens with a named, keyboard-reachable Expand button ahead of the panel's own content (issue #636) - Tab into the flyout and activate it with Enter or Space to restore the panel to a normal docked header, moving focus to that header's own collapse-toggle; this is a separate control from the rail button, so opening the flyout to look at a panel never accidentally undocks it.
mobile: Below 640px a splitter tree cannot show real panels, so the dock draws every open panel in reading order as one tab strip with one panel visible; the strip scrolls sideways rather than wrapping onto a second row, the same as a narrow group's tab list. The layout document is untouched, so widening the window restores the arrangement.
